quick.topic: Write down what each event means
quick.summary: Why nobody trusts an event nobody defined, and three things to write for each one.
quick.takeaway: Name, when it fires, what it carries.

parts.title: Write down what each event means

beats.line: Is checkout started the button tap or the page load? Nobody knows.
Then every chart built on it is a guess.
Three things for each event. First, its exact name.
Second, the moment it fires, in plain words.
Third, the details it carries, like price or plan.
Is a document really worth the time?
Less time than the next argument about what a number means.
Checkout started fires when the payment page finishes loading. It carries the cart total.
Now the next analyst knows without asking.

quiz.question: Which line best documents an event?
options: Fires when the payment page finishes loading; carries cart total
quiz.explanation: It says exactly when the event fires and what it carries, so anyone can read numbers built on it.

quiz.question: An event name on its own is enough for everyone to know when it fires.
quiz.explanation: Names can be read many ways. Writing the moment it fires removes the guesswork.
